caption: Before · the old Notebook pane that 0.3.0 still draws around the new editor
1 · The Notebook: one side list (Recents, Pinned, Folders, Pages as a tree; Templates and Trash at the foot) and the page to its right. No tabs, no cards
Directions for where a page opens
3 · Hover a row: ▸ at the left, ⋯ and + at the right, only under the pointer
4 · ▸ opens the pages inside, 12 px in; a page can hold pages to any depth
10–12 · The page list is a table, one line a page: Name, Folder, Edited, Created; a header sorts; "Open" on hover; filters above (filters-v2)
13 · A click anywhere opens the page in place: it replaces what was shown; its row lights; ← → walk back
14 · From a list in a page, a row opens as a side peek; ⤢ opens it full, Esc closes
15 · Ctrl+click opens beside: two pages at most; a third replaces the right one
17 · New page opens in place, title focused; it is at the top of Pages at once; left with no words, it is not kept
18–19 · Move to Trash: the row leaves, the previous page opens, one toast with Undo for 30 seconds
20–21 · Trash is a popover beside the side list, not a view: search, restore ↺, erase 🗑; Esc or a click outside leaves it, nothing else changes
22–24 · A trashed page opens read-only under a band: Restore, or Erase now (asks first)
25–29 · Right-click or ⋯ on a row: the one menu, searchable, shortcuts at the right
30 · The Notebook as one pane beside the reader: the side list and the page inside it; no hidden tab is ever made
32 · Narrow: the side list fills the pane; a page opens over it with ‹ back to the list
36 · Only the focused empty line hints; the other empty lines and the space under the page say nothing
